answer: An agent marketplace requires each active identity to lock a $100 bond for 90 days before it can bid on jobs, whether buying a mirror, mapping a dune, or sourcing saffron. Each identity gets the same daily bid limit, so creating aliases does not unlock free bidding capacity: operating 1,000 fake agents requires $100,000 locked up for three months. The defense makes a sybil swarm costly through capital requirements and foregone use of those funds.
